test_title: PYST 43 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Cut the blue wire all at once; otherwise, you have to throw the entire thing out of the house with your maximum strength.

options.text: Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to throw out of the house with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.
Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out with your maximum strength of the house by you.

solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the imperative form, and the passive voice of an imperative sentence typically begins with "Let."
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject.
 
• The correct structure for the passive voice in this sentence is: **Let + object + be + past participle**.
 
• The second part of the sentence, "you have to throw the entire thing out of the house with your maximum strength," is converted to passive voice as "the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength."

Correct sentence: *Let the blue wire be cut all at once; otherwise, the entire thing has to be thrown out of the house by you with your maximum strength*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Passive Voice Structures:**

 
 
• **Imperative Active Voice:** Cut the wire. → **Passive Voice:** Let the wire be cut.
 
• **Present Simple Active Voice:** She throws the ball. → **Passive Voice:** The ball is thrown by her.
 
• **Future Simple Active Voice:** He will complete the project. → **Passive Voice:** The project will be completed by him.
 
 
 
• **Note:** Always ensure the correct placement of "by" and the subject when converting sentences to passive voice.
